headline: Showers and maybe a thunderstorm this afternoon and evening, a dry break Tuesday–Wednesday, then a stronger, windier storm Thursday.

sections.title: Today & tonight
sections.text: A weak system brings showers to the coast from late morning, spreading inland in the afternoon. The heaviest bursts (and a stray thunderstorm) are most likely between about 4 and 10 PM. Rain totals are light — generally a tenth to a quarter inch — with San Diego County getting more than Orange County. Showers clear out overnight.

sections.title: Tuesday–Wednesday
sections.text: Dry, but not warm: highs run a few degrees below normal, in the 60s at the coast, with chilly nights near 50.

sections.title: Thursday
sections.text: The main event of the week. A stronger system brings more rain and wind than today's — roughly half an inch around San Diego, about an inch in Orange County, and more in the mountains. Gusts of 25–30 mph at the coast; much stronger in mountain passes. Snow is possible above about 7,000 feet.

sections.title: Friday through the weekend
sections.text: Drying out and a little warmer Friday and Saturday. Another, weaker system may arrive Sunday or Monday, but forecasters have low confidence in its timing.

coast: High surf continues: 6–8 ft with sets near 10 ft on west-facing beaches through Tuesday night (High Surf Advisory until 4 AM Wednesday). Another swell arrives Thursday afternoon and likely keeps surf dangerous into the weekend. Rough seas for boaters this afternoon through Wednesday morning and again Thursday.
watch_for: Brief downpours or a thunderstorm at the coast this evening.
Thursday's storm tracking a bit farther north, which would mean less rain here.
confidence: Moderate to high for Thursday's storm; low for anything Sunday–Monday.
